newsitem.title: UK: Frankfurt hits record, all Eurobourses strong.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt hits record, all Eurobourses strong.

text.p: German stocks hit a new trading peak on Thursday as unemployment data eased inflation worries and all European bourses recovered from the previous day's losses to show gains.
On currency markets, the dollar weakened against the yen but was steady against the mark after a Bundesbank council meeting held German interest rates steady.

Frankfurt was in sparkling form, with floor trade surging to an intra-day high of 2914.61 points, eclipsing the previous best of 2895.19 set only two days ago. Computerised deals also hit a record of 2916.16 points.
The recent bull run in Frankfurt and other European centres has been fuelled by the strength of the dollar lately which markets see as helping exporting sectors.
Thursday's surge came as government figures showed German unemployment climbed to a post-unification record in November, rising 50,000 to 4.1 million, suggesting subdued inflationary pressures.
"It's really quite substantially more than expected," James Stewart of SE Banken in London told Reuters Financial Television.

Analysts disagreed on whether the data meant the economy was slowing but the market interpreted the figures as indicating interest rates would not rise and that exporters would not lose the mark's competitive edge against the dollar.
This assessment was shown to be accurate when the Bundesbank said that its its policy-making council had decided to leave the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks perked up by 0.7 percent after Wednesday's falls but trading was nervous ahead of important U.S. economic figures on employment due on Friday.
"There wasn't a huge amount of business around yesterday and I don't expect there to be much around today," said one dealer. "A lot depends on those (U.S. November employment) numbers tomorrow."

The market was slightly unsettled by volatility on currency and commodity markets, and worries about whether the last two day's poor performance on Wall Street signalled the end of its record-breaking pace.

Although the Dow closed with a 19.75-point loss at 6,422.94, on Wednesday, some remained optimistic. "I don't think buyers are ready to capitulate at the moment. There's too much cash around," a London dealer said.
Paris stocks showed a 0.3 precent rise after a weak start. Lagardere slipped further after a government decision on Wednesday to suspend the Thomson SA privatisation.
The dollar was looking a bit weaker after its recent strong performance, culminating in hitting a 23-month high against the mark on Tuesday.
The U.S. currency slid nearly a yen and dealers said trade was cautious ahead of a TV appearance by Japanese Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara later on Thursday.

"There are a number of rumours of what Sakakibara is going to say," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International. "No one really knows if this will be a bland interview or if he has something specific to say."
The dollar suffered in overnight trade after remarks from former vice finance minister Makoto Utsumi that the Bank of Japan was seeking an increase in interest rates as soon as possible.

"There is a lot of speculation about a shift in Japanese monetary policy," said a Swiss bank dealer here. "Although it doesn't seem warranted now, higher rates in Japan are on the cards, and the betting is that it could be sooner rather than later."
The dollar was marginally lower against the mark compared to the levels seen in late trading on Wednesday but generally holding firm after the Bundesbank council meeting.
CURRENCIES AT 1215 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 112.68 yen and 1.5615 marks against 113.28 yen and 1.5638 marks in late Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1215 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 29.8 points at 4,075.0.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 6.43 points at 2,315.08.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 43.64 points at 2,909.97.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $368.30 an ounce, compared to $369.95 at Wednesday's close. Silver was at $4.72, down 10 cents.
